sources.title: Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in A/B Testing
sources.claim_scope: Sample ratio mismatch as an experiment-quality warning requiring diagnosis before effect interpretation.
sources.evidence_summary: Microsoft's primary experimentation publication describes assignment, execution, logging, and analysis defects that can create mismatch and advocates checking mismatch before trusting effects.

sources.title: R: Power Calculations for Two-Sample Test for Proportions
sources.claim_scope: Two-sample proportion power calculation arguments and per-group definition of n.
sources.evidence_summary: R stats documentation defines p1, p2, significance, power, and n per group; used as a reference convention, not as evidence of observed business conversion rates.

sources.title: About Conversion Lift
sources.claim_scope: Google Conversion Lift controlled comparison and account availability limits.
sources.evidence_summary: Google states Conversion Lift is not available to every account and describes exposed and control comparisons plus incremental conversion metrics.

sources.title: Evaluation best practices
sources.claim_scope: Task-specific datasets and evaluations for AI workflow quality.
sources.evidence_summary: Primary OpenAI evaluation guidance supports explicit evaluation instead of impression-only model assessment; no claim of measured ClimbOS model superiority is derived.

sources.title: AI features and your website
sources.claim_scope: Google's primary documentation for website participation in its AI search features.
sources.evidence_summary: Used for the limited claim that AI-mediated search has website documentation and changing platform requirements. No guaranteed traffic or ranking tactic is claimed.

sources.title: Get started with attribution
sources.claim_scope: Attribution assigns touchpoint credit under a model and reporting scope.
sources.evidence_summary: Google Analytics describes attribution models and credit assignment. The book's commercial recommendation distinguishes that operational reporting from a causal incrementality claim.

sources.title: Increasing Access — LinkedIn Marketing
sources.claim_scope: LinkedIn API product access, tiers, and permissions require verification for the proposed action.
sources.evidence_summary: Primary versioned LinkedIn documentation describes product-specific access and permissions. No claim is made that ClimbOS currently has approved API access.

sources.title: Idempotency Keys — Resend
sources.claim_scope: Provider support for idempotency keys in sending requests.
sources.evidence_summary: Resend documents request deduplication via idempotency keys. Application workflow state, reconciliation, and permission requirements are original proposed architecture guidance.

limitations: Primary documentation was checked on October 19, 2026; future platform changes require revalidation.
Null publication dates indicate no verified publication date was recorded; retrieval date is not publication date.
No live advertising account, customer analytics, production repository, or provider permission was inspected.
All numerical business cases are hypothetical teaching scenarios and not Formkit or ClimbOS observations.
Formula examples use stated simplifying assumptions; unsupported designs require specialist review.
Architecture and playbook names are proposed logical mappings, not claims of implemented production capability.
Source material is narrowly summarized; the extensive applied frameworks and cases are original synthesis.
